new_rows.eligibility_notes: PIs and Co-PIs must hold an earned doctorate in an academic discipline or professional field and be affiliated with a non-profit organization or public/governmental institution (university, school district, research facility or 501(c)(3)).
new_rows.specific_topic: education research broadly conceived, across education, anthropology, philosophy, psychology, sociology, law, economics, history or neuroscience

new_rows.funder: Spencer Foundation / National Academy of Education
new_rows.stated_purpose: Supports individuals whose dissertations show potential for bringing fresh and productive perspectives to the history, theory, analysis or practice of formal or informal education anywhere in the world.
new_rows.eligibility_notes: Doctoral students across a wide range of disciplines; the dissertation topic must concern education, formal or informal, anywhere in the world.
new_rows.status_evidence: “The deadline for this competitive program is in the fall of each year”; the 2026 competition closes 8 October 2026.
new_rows.notes: Added 2026-09-18 (P2). Administered with the National Academy of Education.

new_rows.program_name: Research-Practice Partnerships: Collaborative Research for Educational Change

new_rows.eligibility_notes: PIs and Co-PIs must hold an earned doctorate in an academic discipline or professional field and be affiliated with a non-profit organization or public/governmental institution (university, school district, research facility or 501(c)(3)).
new_rows.specific_topic: education research broadly conceived, across education, anthropology, philosophy, psychology, sociology, law, economics, history or neuroscience

new_rows.stated_purpose: Supports career development for promising early-career researchers through five-year research and mentoring plans that significantly expand their expertise in new disciplines, methods and content areas.
new_rows.typical_award_size: $425,000 total, including up to 7.5% indirect costs
new_rows.eligibility_window: Within 7 years of doctoral degree conferral, or of completing the first residency for applicants in medicine
new_rows.eligibility_notes: Applicants must hold career-ladder positions with a pathway to research advancement and be nominated by their institution. The Foundation makes grants to tax-exempt organizations, not to individuals, and defers to the applying organization's criteria for who may act as PI. Research on the causes, extent or consequences of inequality is out of scope; the study must examine a response to it.
new_rows.specific_topic: programmes, policies or practices to reduce inequality in academic, social, behavioural or economic outcomes of young people ages 5-25 in the United States, or improving the use of research evidence
new_rows.selectivity: four to six Scholars selected each year
new_rows.status_evidence: “The 2026 competition is now closed. Dates for the next competition will be posted in January 2027”.
new_rows.notes: Added 2026-09-18 (P2). Limited submission: “Major divisions of an institution (e.g., College of Arts and Sciences, Medical School) may nominate only one applicant each year”.

new_rows.stated_purpose: Provides support for PhD holders to conduct research projects aligned with RSF's research priorities and special initiatives.
new_rows.typical_award_size: Up to $200,000; awards above $75,000 include 15% indirect costs
new_rows.eligibility_notes: Applicants must hold a PhD. Awards up to $75,000 are made under presidential authority; larger awards require trustee approval.
new_rows.specific_topic: social, economic, political and behavioural science aligned with RSF's stated research priorities and special initiatives
new_rows.status_evidence: RSF's Core Research Grants page is current and describes the programme as providing “up to $200,000 for PhD holders to conduct research projects aligned with RSF's research priorities”. No suspension notice.
new_rows.notes: Added 2026-09-18 (P2). RSF runs several cycles a year and reviews an initial letter of inquiry before inviting a proposal, which is why submission_path is `other`. The grant period was not stated on the programme page.

new_rows.program_name: RSF Visiting Researchers Fellowship (Visiting Scholars Program)
new_rows.stated_purpose: A residential fellowship offering scholars in the social, economic, political and behavioural sciences time to pursue data analysis and writing in residence at the Foundation's New York headquarters.
new_rows.eligibility_notes: Applicants must hold a PhD and be at least two years beyond conferral at the time of application. Residency at RSF's New York City headquarters is required.
new_rows.specific_topic: social, economic, political and behavioural science aligned with RSF's core programmes
new_rows.status_evidence: RSF lists an incoming cohort of 20 visiting scholars for 2026-27 and describes the programme as current.
new_rows.notes: Added 2026-09-18 (P2). PROVENANCE: the award amount, the two-years-post-PhD gate and the 25 June 2026 deadline were read through the search index; the programme page itself states none of them. Hence confidence=medium and a blank award_checked.
